title: [11/8/2024] Car ownership in the UK
prompt: The chart below gives information about car ownership in the UK from 1975 to 2005. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The given line graph illustrates the proportions of the population owning one, two, three cars, and of those not owning one in Great Britain from 1975 to 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, possession of automobiles in the UK increased over the thirty-year period, and having one car remained the most popular throughout the years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: At the start of the period, similar proportions of people had one car and no cars, with figures of 45% and 43%, respectively. Thereafter, both options declined in popularity in the first decade. Over the next twenty years, the percentage of single-car ownership followed an upward trend, finally ending up at 45% in 2005. After falling from 43% in 1975 to 25% in 1985, the proportion of non-car owners continued to decline more steadily, and at the end of the period, 22% of individuals did not own a car.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding households with multiple cars, only about 6% owned two cars in 1975, while the figure for three-car ownership was negligible at roughly 2%. Both categories showed gradual increases over the next three decades, with two-car households rising to about 18% and three-car families reaching nearly 10% by 2005.
